key_insight: AdaPCLA improves longitudinal EHR generation for rare conditions by adaptively calibrating logits so tail-event co-occurrence patterns are better preserved.
clinical_relevance: More faithful synthetic EHRs could support privacy-preserving method development and analysis for underrepresented patient subgroups.
method: Uses a data distribution-aware training strategy with simulated annealing to internalize prior knowledge.
Applies adaptive prior-calibrated logit adjustment to better model rare-code relationships.
Includes training-free zero-shot distribution control for adapting generation to different clinical populations.
evidence_signal: On real-world MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV data, the method improved tail plausibility and downstream utility, including large TailPairSeen gains over HALO and a 3.5% F1 improvement for zero-shot cross-population adaptation.
watch_item: Performance gains are reported on benchmark EHR datasets, so generalization and calibration may still need validation in other hospitals, coding systems, and rare-event settings.
paper_title: AdaPCLA: Adaptive Prior-Calibrated Logit Adjustment for Long-Tailed Longitudinal EHR Generation
